subject: Promo wrangle: combining accelerator credits with Dedicated conversion
messages:
From: Kate Lang <kate@seedfoundry.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ops@seedfoundry.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — accelerator credits + Dedicated conversion

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We loved the latency profile and the cost controls — exactly what our platform team needs. Two quick questions from the program ops side: 1) we have a pool of $25k in accelerator/promotional credits that the finance team would prefer to apply toward an initial Dedicated commitment, rather than letting them expire; 2) the legal team is asking if there is a documented conversion path from free credits to prepaid/reserved capacity (how are credits treated in the contract).

Attached is a one-pager on our cohort (seedfoundry_program_summary.pdf) so you can see usage expectations (mostly embeddings and moderate chat throughput). Can Redwood carve those promo credits into a deal that feeds into a Dedicated commit, or do they strictly stay as hosted/one-off credits?

We are on a short schedule — would appreciate a quick sketch of options and the ops/legal implications.

Best,
Kate Lang
Head of Programs, SeedFoundry
[Attachment: seedfoundry_program_summary.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Kate Lang <kate@seedfoundry.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — accelerator credits + Dedicated conversion

Hi Kate — great to hear from you and congrats on the strong cohort. Short answer: we can be flexible, but there are accounting and contract steps to make this clean. I pulled in Ben (pricing) and Irene (contracts/ops) to outline two pragmatic options below.

Option A — Credit-apply to first-month invoice (simple, fast):
- Promo credits applied as a one-time credit against initial invoices for Hosted API or Dedicated onboarding fees.
- Accounting treat credits as contra-revenue; we record usage on normal invoicing and net to zero up to $25k.
- Legal: minimal contract work — credits reflected in a one-page addendum noting applied credit amount and expiry behavior.
- Pros: fast, preserves ability to move to Dedicated quickly.
- Cons: credits do not convert to a prepayment that counts toward committed GPU-months if you choose prepaid Dedicated later (depending on finance rules).

Option B — Credits converted to a committed discount for Dedicated (structured; requires more ops):
- Credits moved into a committed-rate carveout: we sign an addendum converting $25k of promo value into a staged discount applied across the first N months of a Dedicated commit.
- Contract: requires an amendment that specifies how the promo value is amortized across committed billing and includes audit trail for compliance.
- Billing: we will need SeedFoundry PO/ack to reflect the conversion and a short acceptance signoff.
- Pros: preserves value against committed spend, aligns incentives for conversion.
- Cons: takes 4–7 business days to finalize with finance/legal; slightly more effort for your ops.

Next steps I suggest: Ben can build a simple price sketch for both flows (showing effective blended unit cost), and Irene can draft the small addendum language for Option B if you prefer that route. If you want to talk live, I can slot 30 minutes tomorrow afternoon.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf (PDF, 860KB)]
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Kate Lang <kate@seedfoundry.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — accelerator credits + Dedicated conversion

Thanks Jonas — adding the numbers below so Kate's team can see the delta. I ran a quick model against the usage profile in your one-pager.

If you stay Hosted and we apply credits to invoices (Option A):
- Estimated monthly tokens: 40M generation-equivalent tokens + 250k embedding units.
- Typical hosted rate (example): $0.0018 / generation-k / $0.0009 / embedding unit (illustrative).
- $25k covers ~13–15k generation-k equivalents or ~28M embeddings depending on mix.

If you convert to Dedicated and we amortize credits as a conversion discount (Option B):
- Example Dedicated commit: 1 x A100-like pool (reserved), monthly base $18k.
- Convert $25k into a staged discount: e.g., $8k off month 1, $8.5k off month 2, $8.5k off month 3 (illustrative).
- Effective blended month 1 cost after credit: $10k; month 2/3: ~$9.5k.

Operational asks from our side for Option B:
- Signed addendum stating conversion mechanics and timeline.
- PO or email confirmation from SeedFoundry finance acknowledging amortization schedule.
- Internal billing ticket to route the credit application to the Dedicated ledger.

Irene — can you confirm the minimal language we should use for the addendum (and whether we need finance legal sign-off for a $25k recharacterization)?

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sow-dedicated-conversion.docx (DOCX, 120KB)]
From: Kate Lang <kate@seedfoundry.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, ops@seedfoundry.com
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — accelerator credits + Dedicated conversion

Thanks all — this is exactly the clarity we needed. SeedFoundry prefers Option B (convert into a staged Dedicated discount) so we can lock predictable capacity for the cohort.

A few ops notes:
- We'll send an official PO once we have the addendum language.
- Our procurement team needs the amortization schedule (your illustrative numbers are fine — they just need the table).
- Can Redwood confirm the latest date by which the addendum must be signed for credits to remain valid? We have an internal expiry rule of credits after 9 months from issuance.

If you can turn around a 1–2 page addendum and an amortization table by Monday EOD, we'll move forward. Happy to accept a brief call Friday to speed this.

Best,
Kate Lang
Head of Programs, SeedFoundry
